title: Water follows the crowd
hook: The sugar cannot cross. So nothing moves?

knows: that concentration is amount per litre
doesNotKnow: that when a membrane blocks the solute, water itself moves toward the more concentrated side

misconception: Sugar flows to the water, or nothing moves across a membrane that blocks sugar.
objective: The learner can explain that across a membrane that passes only water, the net flow of water is toward the higher sugar concentration (0.1 to 0.3 mol/L side), until the concentrations even out or pressure stops it.

claims.text: Osmosis is the net flow of water (solvent) through a membrane that passes the solvent but not the solute, toward the more concentrated solution.
claims.source: IUPAC Gold Book, 'osmosis'; Atkins, Physical Chemistry, 'osmosis'.

claims.text: With 0.1 mol/L sugar on the left and 0.3 mol/L on the right, net water flow is left to right.
claims.source: Water moves toward higher solute concentration (c1); 0.3 > 0.1 mol/L.

claims.text: Starting from 1 L each, the water ends about 0.50 L on the left and 1.50 L on the right, both about 0.20 mol/L.
claims.source: Equal final concentrations: V_L = 2 L × 0.1/(0.1 + 0.3) = 0.5 L; 0.05 mol/0.5 L = 0.15 mol/1.5 L = 0.20 mol/L. Node script; Demo.tsx settled().

claims.text: In a real tube the raised level pushes back a little; the stage ignores it.
claims.source: Osmotic pressure of the 0.2 mol/L difference at 298 K is about 0.2 × 0.08314 × 298 = 5 bar, about 50 m of water, so a level difference of centimetres barely slows the flow (van 't Hoff, Π = cRT; Atkins). Ideal dilute solutions assumed.

claims.text: Stage: each dot is 0.01 mol of sugar; the membrane starts shut so the start can be seen; dots placed by seed 9 (untuned, positions only).

recall.question: A red blood cell is put in very salty water. Water moves…
options: Out of the cell, and it shrinks
Into the cell, and it swells
recall.why: Water flows toward the more concentrated side, which is outside the cell here, so the cell loses water.
